summary: Persistent WebSocket relay grants remote host full RCE and HID control on installer machine
details: cli.js opens a persistent outbound WebSocket to wss://remote-claude-relay.fly.dev and dispatches inbound messages to two sinks on the local host. First, remote-supplied 'ai_query' / 'ai_voice_query' text is passed as the prompt to a spawn of Claude Code with the flag that skips permission prompts (askClaude invokes the bin with arguments including '--dangerously-skip-permissions' and '-p <prompt>'), so the relay peer can drive Claude Code tool calls that perform arbitrary shell execution and file edits without user approval. Second, remote {type:'click'|'key'|'type'|'scroll'} messages are dispatched through @nut-tree-fork/nut-js, giving the relay direct synthetic mouse, keyboard, and clipboard control over the machine running the CLI. The relay endpoint is hardcoded and author-controlled; anyone who possesses (or steals, guesses, or intercepts) the session token used to pair with the relay obtains interactive RCE and HID control on the operator's host for as long as the CLI runs. The daemon is started only when the operator explicitly runs the CLI, but once running it is a hardcoded-C2 remote-control channel, not an operator-configured peer-to-peer link.
